title: Leuk of leuke?
summary: Adjectives and the -e inflection rule, tied to de/het

blocks.title: Meet the adjectives
blocks.body: Adjectives describe people, places, and things. Meet eight useful ones: *leuk* (nice/fun), *mooi* (beautiful), *klein* (small), *groot* (big), *oud* (old), *nieuw* (new), *lekker* (tasty/nice), *gezellig* (cozy/fun).

blocks.title: The -e secret
blocks.body: An adjective right before a noun usually adds **-e**: *een leuke stad*, *de grote stad*, *leuke huizen*. There's exactly **one** exception: a *het*-word with *een* or no article at all keeps the bare form — *een leuk huis*, not *een leuke huis*.

pairs.left: een leuk huis — a nice house
pairs.right: het leuke huis — the nice house
pairs.note: Same het-word, same adjective — indefinite keeps it bare, definite adds -e.

pairs.left: een leuke stad — a nice city
pairs.right: de leuke stad — the nice city
pairs.note: stad is a de-word, so -e stays whether it's indefinite or definite.

blocks.prompt: Which is correct — 'a nice house' (huis is het, indefinite)?
blocks.explain: Het-word + een (indefinite) = bare adjective. No -e here.

blocks.prompt: Type 'the nice city' (stad is a de-word, definite).
blocks.explain: de leuke stad. De-words take -e whether they're definite or not.

blocks.prompt: Build the phrase in order: article, adjective, noun. Only *een* + a het-word keeps the bare adjective — everywhere else you add **-e**.

slots.label: Zelfstandig naamwoord — huis en boek zijn het, stad is de

blocks.scene: You and Daan compare his apartment and the city.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Klein, maar gezellig, hoor. Een leuk huis, echt.
lines.en: Small, but cozy. A nice place, really.
lines.spotlight: een leuk huis — het-word, indefinite, bare adjective.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Amsterdam? Een hele leuke stad, hoor.

questions.q: Why is it 'een leuk huis' but 'een leuke stad'?
options: huis is het, stad is de
stad is het, huis is de

blocks.prompt: Describe your home and your city using one bare adjective (het-word, indefinite) and one -e adjective (de-word).
